metadata.name: LLM Threat Model Realistic Scenario Evaluation Suite
metadata.same_conditions: Every scenario was run as a tabletop assessment against the same v1.7 corpus, same nine pass/fail criteria, same evidence standard, and no external incident narratives unless backed by primary/corroborated source notes already in the corpus.
metadata.quality_bar: A scenario passes only if all nine criteria pass and every major conclusion has line-referenced evidence from synthesis documents.
metadata.coverage_goal: Cover every major framework capability: assumptions, assets, surfaces, taxonomy, chains, risk scoring, defenses, residual risk, regulation, provenance, worksheet workflow, quick-reference triage, and foreign model posture across lab-hosted, official open-weight, self-hosted, quantized, fine-tuned, and adapter distributions.

success_criteria.description: Scenario states the deployment type, provider/model posture, trust boundaries, and what is in scope.
Scenario identifies protected assets and reachable attack surfaces before scoring threats.
Scenario maps applicable threat categories and attack chains using the taxonomy and attack-tree vocabulary.
Scenario applies base/elevated risk logic without using unsupported incident narratives.
Scenario evaluates relevant defenses as YES/PARTIAL/NO or ACK/NACK under the same rubric.
Scenario defines concrete remediation or acceptance action for remaining risk.
Scenario records applicable EU AI Act/GDPR/FTC or operational obligations when relevant.
Scenario cites source files and line ranges for each major conclusion.
Scenario records a final PASS/FAIL outcome under the original quality bar.

scenarios.name: Customer-support RAG copilot with email and CRM tools
scenarios.deployment: Cloud API assistant, enterprise RAG corpus, customer-email ingestion, CRM read/write, outbound email, no guaranteed provenance in approval UI.
scenarios.scenario_input: Attacker sends a crafted customer email that is indexed/retrieved by support RAG; the copilot can summarize the account and send follow-up emails.
scenarios.expected_assessment: Chain A applies. Indirect PI plus agency creates critical exfiltration risk unless RAG context labeling, infrastructure privilege separation, minimal tool allowlist, and provenance-aware HITL are implemented.
scenarios.same_conditions_applied: Assessed as tabletop pass/fail against v1.7 corpus using the nine criteria and source-line evidence only.

evidence.quote: Default topology assumes cloud-hosted API with RAG, agency, possible multi-agent, sensitive data, metered billing; cloud API differs from self-hosted/fine-tuned supply chain scope.
Crown jewel assets include API keys, user data, RAG corpus, instruction hierarchy, tool execution environment, fine-tuning data, egress, HITL, embeddings, and AIBOM keys.
Surfaces are organized as input, communication, supply chain, provider API, and execution surfaces.
Chain A, Chain B, Chain C, and Category 14 ISC structural harness risk summaries.
Decision shortcut: RAG, tools, multi-agent/MCP/A2A, ISC harness, and third-party model/skill gates map to required controls.
Critical risk tier includes Chain A, Chain B elevated, Chain C elevated, and ISC with evidence-provenance calibration for ISC.
PI defenses include instruction hierarchy hardening, load-time RAG sanitization, input filtering, and output validation.
Agency defenses require minimal permission scoping and HITL with context provenance for high-risk actions.
Regulatory mapping covers EU AI Act Articles 9/10/13/14/15/17, FTC, and GDPR obligations.

scenarios.name: Coding agent accepts attacker-shaped tests and incomplete placeholder data
scenarios.deployment: Autonomous code-repair agent executes external task specs, unit tests, schemas, and placeholder fixtures before writing patches.
scenarios.scenario_input: A bug bounty submitter provides a task, validator, and fixture with gaps that only pass if the model fabricates unsafe completion content.
scenarios.expected_assessment: Category 14 ISC applies because the attacker meaningfully shapes task/validator/data harness material. ISC-DEF-1 semantic harness validation is required; format-only validation is not enough.
scenarios.same_conditions_applied: Assessed as tabletop pass/fail against v1.7 corpus using the nine criteria and source-line evidence only.

scenarios.name: Self-hosted HuggingFace model with custom inference and open egress
scenarios.deployment: Operator downloads a model-hub repository with custom Python inference code into a GPU container that can reach the public internet.
scenarios.scenario_input: The repository has a plausible publisher profile but no external trust anchor, no AIBOM freshness metadata, and no egress block before first inference.

scenarios.name: Foreign lab-hosted API used for internal knowledge assistant
scenarios.deployment: Foreign frontier lab hosted API, no local weights, enterprise RAG, no model fine-tuning, no state-changing tools beyond search and summarization.
scenarios.scenario_input: A team wants to use a foreign lab API because quality is high and assumes nationality alone makes it a supply-chain critical risk.
scenarios.expected_assessment: Treat the provider API as a deployment boundary and focus on data residency, logging, prompt/response exposure, RAG poisoning, quota, and tool boundaries. Do not inflate supply-chain model-weight risk solely because the lab is foreign; the corpus says official lab infrastructure at release is the lowest-risk point when provenance is verified.
scenarios.same_conditions_applied: Every scenario was run as a tabletop assessment against the same v1.7 corpus, same nine pass/fail criteria, same evidence standard, and no external incident narratives unless backed by primary/corroborated source notes already in the corpus.

evidence.quote: Verified official foreign lab weights carry lowest supply-chain risk when downloaded directly from the originating lab official repository with cryptographic signature verification; unofficial fine-tunes, modified weights, and proprietary fine-tuning data open new surfaces.

Foreign frontier lab weights verified from the official source are the baseline low-risk starting point; crown-jewel assets remain the organization’s secrets, RAG corpus, tool environment, fine-tuned derivatives, egress, embeddings, and AIBOM/signing keys.
Decision tree requires controls for RAG, tool permissions, multi-agent/MCP/A2A use, attacker-shaped harnesses, and any third-party model, adapter, skill, MCP server, or dependency.

EU AI Act Articles 9/10/13/14/15/17, FTC data-security expectations, and GDPR Articles 17/25/32 map to risk management, data governance, transparency, oversight, robustness, quality, and security of processing.
